title: unify terraform private state layout + gpu node pools + iam + vpc networking (state migration)
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: private deployments have accumulated multiple ad-hoc Terraform state layouts and duplicated modules for GPU node pools, IAM roles, and VPC networking. This PR unifies the state layout, centralizes GPU node pool and IAM modules, and introduces a compatibility shim and state migration guide. Goals: 1) Provide a single canonical state layout for Private installer customers, 2) Reduce duplication across environments (GCP/AWS), 3) Make future module upgrades and rollbacks safer by defining clear backwards-compatible APIs. Summary of changes: - Introduce 'modules/private_state' which normalizes remote state keys and module naming. - Add 'modules/gpu_node_pool' (GKE/EC2 variants) with configurable GPU type, image, taints, and node-label mapping used by private deployments. - Consolidate IAM roles into 'modules/private_iam' with least-privilege defaults and optional escalation policies for support. - Update 'modules/networking' to export consistent subnetwork and route names and to support shared VPC configs. - Add migration scripts and documented terraform state mv sequences to move existing customer state to the new layout; include dry-run examples. - Add a compatibility layer in root terraform that maps old names to new modules for one release cycle. - Update Helm chart values used by the installer to reference the new state keys. Backwards compatibility & migration: default behavior is backwards-compatible at apply-time thanks to the compatibility layer, but teams operating with remote state backends MUST run the provided migration script (scripts/migrate-state.sh) and follow the documented state-move steps for any manual state backends. The migration is a one-time operation per workspace. Testing: tested on internal staging and on two customer replica workspaces (GCP us-west1, AWS us-east-1) including plan/apply, destroy, and drift detection. See CI for matrix details. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for Terraform modules (kitchen-terraform) - [x] integration test: staging AWS/GCP - [x] migration docs + scripts - [x] documented rollback steps - [x] reviewers addressed comments Rollout plan: stage rollout on a per-customer basis: 1) create migration branch and run terraform plan against a copy backend, 2) run migrate-state.sh in read-only dry-run, 3) apply migration off-hours with on-call present, 4) monitor infra/installer health dashboards, 5) optionally roll back by reversing state-moves using recorded backups. Related: ENG-9421, ENG-9536, SUP-1245.

release_notes: Unify Terraform state layout for Private deployments; add centralized GPU node pool and IAM modules; migration script included. Customers with existing remote state must follow the migration guide. See notes for rollback steps.
migration_instructions: See scripts/migrate-state.sh and examples/private-deployments/migration.md. High level: 1) backup remote state (terraform state pull > backup.json), 2) run scripts/migrate-state.sh --dry-run to see planned state moves, 3) run scripts/migrate-state.sh to perform state mv operations (this runs terraform state mv commands under the hood), 4) run 'terraform plan' in the new layout and verify zero-diff. For manual state backends run the explicit terraform state mv commands listed in migration.md. Keep a copy of the old state file for rollback.
notes: Compatibility shim will be removed in next major release after customer migrations complete
Ops: schedule migrations during maintenance windows; migration takes ~5-20min depending on state size
